answer: Randomness-gated enrollment windows. Each epoch, a verifiable random function over the prior block hash opens short registration windows at unpredictable times; only agents active within the window can enroll, and late or batched attempts are rejected at the ridge of the deadline. Because window timing is unpredictable, an attacker cannot precompute or pre-position identities, so each accepted sybil requires real-time presence, sustained infrastructure, and forfeited idle capacity—costs scaling with attempts, not identities. The honest summit is cheap; the attack pearl is not.
